page.layout: One printed page. Running text in one column, with marginal notes in the right margin. Below the text: a signature mark "Q" at the left and a section heading "XI. Dubium" at the right. The left strip of the scan is the edge of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: præceptione fola pendet utraque illa vis, quam Legi nelle diximus, dirigendi scilicet actiones & obligandi conscientias subditorum. Habet enim subditus sufficientem normam secundum quam dirigere debet actiones suas, & ad cujus observationem, nisi velit officio suo deesse, astringitur in Conscientiâ, simulac refcierit legitimum superiorem suum, hoc vel illud lege præcepisse, sive sit illi legi appositá aliqua pœnâ, sive non. Non ergo ex naturâ ipsius legis, quæ in mera præceptione consistit, exurgit hæc pœnam apponendi necessitas: sed, (ut legis præceptio quæ nuda non {'}sufficeret, suum cum vigore fortiatur effectum, ex duplici alia hypothesi: subjecti nempe, & finis. Expedit enim ut leges sanctissimæ observentur, quæ est hypothesis ex parte finis: suppositá tamen humani cordis innatâ pravitate (quæ est altera hypothesis ex parte subjecti) fieri vix ac ne vix poteft, quin contemptui habeantur vel utilissimæ leges (quæ est plerorumque mortalium quâ negligentiâ, quâ pervivacia,) ni {2}metu saltem contineantur utcunque in officio, qui ludos faciunt Conscientiæ dictamen. Hinc factum, (ex duplici inquam hac hypothesi) ut Reipubl. salutare, & sibi necessarium semper judicarint prudentissimi quique Legislatores, fancire pœnis legum observantiam. Idque Dei ipsius exemplo, cui visus est eam quam primam dedit homini legem, non sine pœnæ interminatione edicere, Gen. 3. Aliquot forrassis boni cives, quorum parcissima ubique feges est, solâ officii conscientiâ, patriæque & virtutis amore adductí, etsi nulla esset propositá pœnâ, ultrò legibus obtemperarent; aft plurima turba solâ formidine pœnæ adiguntur ad officium faciendum. Patet igitur quæ sit in condendis legibus pœnarum constituendarum necessitas.

page.notes: Marginal notes, right margin, in reading order: "Tacitè permittitur, quàm fine ultione prohibetur." (marked '); "Tert. l. contr. Marcion. 26"; "Qui ratione traduci ad meliora non poffunt, folo metu continentur." (marked 2, printed "Qui ratione traduci ad meliora non poffunt, folo metu contisentur" in the scan, transcribed with the word "continentur"); "Quintil. 12; Instit. 7." The note marks ' and 2 are printed in the text at "sufficeret" and "metu". The notes are placed at their lines, not in the text. Doubtful readings: "hypothesi" and "subjecti" are printed with a long s and may be slightly different in the scan; "Gen. 3." and the numbers in the margin are read from a small, blurred print. Section heading "XI. Dubium" is treated as a level 2 part title. The top word "præceptione" is a fragment at the left edge and is continued from the previous page.
